name: enterpriseops-docs
description: The EnterpriseOps Command Center documentation index. Shaped like an MCP resources/list answer so a documentation endpoint can serve the team's own notes to an assistant, with the extra fields a reviewer needs: purpose, module, lastVerified and the decisions each document records.
notes: Paths are relative to the project folder. The application reads this file back (DocumentationIndexService) and verifies that every path resolves on disk; a listed path that does not resolve is a 404 the endpoint would return.
No network call is made anywhere in this application. 'MCP-ready' describes the shape of this file, not a running server.

resources.title: AI prompt library
resources.purpose: The project-rules header every AI session starts with, and the task prompts that build on it.
decisions: Every session starts from the six project rules.
Rule 5 makes the official documentation the boundary: no undocumented APIs.

resources.title: Generated-code review checklist
resources.purpose: The ten questions asked of every change, generated or not, and what stops a merge.
decisions: One Reject finding stops the change; a warning is a conversation.
A platform member that is not in the documented-API catalog blocks the merge.
A review is signed by a reviewer, never by the author.

resources.title: AI-assisted review patterns
resources.purpose: What goes into an AI session on this project, and what every answer is asked on the way out.
decisions: Generated code is reviewed like junior code.
Accept a suggestion only when someone can explain it without the tool present.

resources.title: AI usage notes
resources.purpose: Which generated code was accepted, by whom and why — including what was rejected.
decisions: PR #214 rev 1 rejected: static session state and two invented APIs.
PR #214 rev 2 accepted: instance service, documented APIs, visible failure path.
Authorization and concurrency code is not drafted by an assistant.

resources.title: Project documentation index (Markdown)
resources.purpose: The human-readable index: every document with its purpose, the decisions it records and the date it was last verified.
decisions: A person browses the Markdown index; a tool retrieves the JSON one.
Every entry carries a purpose written for someone who has never met the team.

resources.title: Project documentation index (MCP resources)
resources.purpose: The machine-readable index a documentation MCP endpoint would serve as resources/list.
decisions: The index lists itself, so a retrieved answer explains where it came from.
Every listed path is verified against disk before the package is called ready.

resources.title: Capstone demo script
resources.purpose: The seven-stop production architecture review, each stop pairing a working screen with a failure path.
decisions: The capstone is delivered as an architecture review, not a feature demo.
Every stop shows a failure path, because the review is about what happens when things go wrong.

resources.title: Architecture defense deck outline
resources.purpose: Twelve slides: one claim, one piece of evidence and one risk each, ending with what is not done.
decisions: A slide without evidence is an opinion.
The last slide is the open items, read out with their owners.

resources.title: Production readiness statement
resources.purpose: What is ready, the four questions answered in writing, the open items with owners and dates, and the sign-off.
decisions: State ownership, security implications, failure paths and production behaviour are explained, not assumed.
Six open items are named with an owner and a date.

resources.title: Capstone architecture diagram
resources.purpose: One picture of the capstone: the session, the layers a command crosses, and the package that ships with it.
decisions: The diagram is the slide-1 evidence of the defense deck.
